cards.text: Here it is, friend: the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar. It's the day the command and edict of King Xerxes of Persia are to be carried out. The enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them on this very day.

cards.question: The enemies of the Jews planned to overpower them on the thirteenth of Adar. How does that plan turn out?

answers.text: It's overturned and the Jews overpower them
It works in every single province
The king calls the whole day off

cards.text: Mordecai, Queen Esther's cousin, had sent out a second edict in the king's name letting the Jews gather and defend themselves (Esther 2:7; 8:10-11). So in every province of King Xerxes, the Jews gather in their cities against those who want to harm them.

cards.question: True or false: Plenty of men in the provinces are able to stand against the Jews that day.
No one can stand against the Jews on the thirteenth of Adar. Why not?

answers.text: The fear of them has fallen on all peoples
The king's own army stands guard over them
Their enemies have all fled the provinces

cards.text: Now the people who run the provinces step in: the satraps, the governors and the king's administrators. That's the WHOLE org chart, friend: the boss, the boss's boss, and the guy the boss's boss is scared of.

cards.question: The satraps, governors and administrators of the provinces get involved on the thirteenth of Adar. What do they do?
The officials of the provinces help the Jews because the fear of ___ had fallen upon them.

cards.text: Mordecai has great power in the palace, and his fame spreads through the provinces as he grows more and more powerful. My career went the OTHER direction, friend: from the counter to the back of the junk drawer, under a takeout menu.
The Jews put their enemies to the sword, and they do as they please to those who hated them. Then the text zooms in on the citadel of Susa.

cards.question: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews kill and destroy ___ men.

cards.text: Among those five hundred, the Jews kill ten men named one by one, from Parshandatha all the way down to Vaizatha. They're the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, the man who had plotted to destroy them (Esther 3:6).

cards.question: The king's letter allowed the Jews to plunder their enemies' possessions (Esther 8:11). True or false: In Susa, the Jews take the plunder.

cards.text: That same day, the number killed in the citadel of Susa is reported to King Xerxes. He tells Queen Esther the count, five hundred men including Haman's ten sons, and asks what the Jews have done in the rest of the provinces.

cards.question: Then King Xerxes asks Queen Esther a question he's asked her before (Esther 5:3; 7:2). What does he want to know?

cards.text: And whatever she asks, he promises it'll be done. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and every time it opened, nobody ever asked, 'Papa, what's your petition?' They just wanted the SCISSORS.

cards.question: Esther asks that the Jews in Susa also get ___ to carry out today's edict.

cards.text: Then comes her second request: that the bodies of Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows.

cards.question: True or false: King Xerxes turns down Esther's requests this time.

cards.text: An edict goes out in Susa, and Haman's ten sons are hanged. Then on the fourteenth of Adar, the Jews in Susa come together again.

cards.question: On the fourteenth of Adar, how many men do the Jews in Susa put to death?

cards.text: Once again, they don't lay a hand on the plunder. Friend, that's DISCIPLINE. I can't walk past a cooling rack without 'quality checking' a cookie.
Out in the rest of the provinces, the Jews assemble to defend themselves and rid themselves of their enemies. They kill 75,000 who hated them.

cards.question: Out in the provinces, the Jews have defeated 75,000 who hated them. What do they do with the plunder?

answers.text: They send it to the king

cards.question: The Jews in the provinces did all this on the thirteenth of Adar. True or false: On the fourteenth they rest and make it a day of feasting and joy.
The Jews in Susa assembled on both the thirteenth and the fourteenth. So they rest on the ___ day of Adar.

cards.text: So that's why the Jews out in the villages keep the fourteenth of Adar as a day of joy and feasting.

cards.question: The village Jews keep the fourteenth of Adar as a holiday. What do they do for one another on it?

answers.text: Read the Law to one another

cards.text: Joy, feasting AND gifts? Friend, I pack cookie boxes all day long and NOBODY has ever sent me one back. But don't hang up your apron yet, because Esther's story isn't done.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only one that uses the passage's own wording ('overturned'), and it is noticeably longer than the two wrong answers. A baker can pick it because it sounds like the Bible, without reasoning about the moment.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The setup rules out a wrong answer. Card 6 says the officials 'step in', and card 7's question says they 'get involved'. Both rule out the wrong answer 'They stay out of it' before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The org-chart joke doesn't map cleanly onto the three titles. 'The boss, the boss's boss, and the guy the boss's boss is scared of' doesn't line up with satraps, governors and administrators in order, and the third tier matches none of them. A reader has to stop and work it out instead of laughing.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Card 11 asks about a line that repeats. 'But they did not lay a hand on the plunder' appears in 9:10, 9:15 and 9:16. Stop 1 card 13 already asks about it at its first appearance (9:10), and stop 2 card 9 tells it again for 9:15. Card 11 asks about it a second time, at its third appearance.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.
